title: Remove Nth Node from End of List
summary: Remove the n-th node counted from the end of a singly linked list and return the resulting head.

contractDetails.constraints: The input has 1–30 nodes with integer values in [0, 100]. n is between 1 and the number of nodes. The input is acyclic.

statement: Remove the n-th node counted from the end of a singly linked list and return the resulting head. n = 1 removes the tail. The judge represents an empty result with an empty array.

examples.explanation: The second node from the tail has value 9.
Counting back three positions removes the head.
Removing the only node leaves an empty list.

constraints: The input has 1–30 nodes with integer values in [0, 100]. n is between 1 and the number of nodes. The input is acyclic.
hints: Conceptual: To unlink the target, it helps to reach the node immediately before it.
Directional: Use a dummy node and maintain a gap between two pointers.
Implementation: Advance the leading pointer n links from the dummy, then move both until the leading pointer is at the tail. Skip the follower's next node.
complexityAnalysis: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space for a list of n nodes. The fixed gap locates the predecessor in one traversal.
